la:adj:tepidus.html:
tĕpĭdus, a, um, adj.
tepeo
,
moderately warm, lukewarm, tepid (cf.: calidus, fervidus).
Lit.: frigidum aliquid et calidum novimus: inter utrumque tepidum est. Si tepido illi plus frigidi ingessero, fiet frigidum: si plus calidi affudero, fiet novissime calidum,; so, calidus tepidusque vapor,: tactus,: lac,: jus,: sol,: brumae,: cruor,: foci,: rogi,; : Notus,: Berenicida,: aqua,; .—Comp.: fastigia tepidiora,: dies,; .—Sup.: cubiculum hieme tepidissimum,. —
Trop., opp. to heat, ardor, lukewarm, cooled, faint, languid, etc.: tepidam recalescere mentem,; so, mens,: ignes,; : adflarant tepidae pectora vestra faces,.—Adv.: tĕpĭdē, tepidly, lukewarmly.
Lit., . — Comp., ; .—*
Trop., without warmth, flatly: tepidissime hoc dicebat,

la:verb:tepeo.gloss: to be warm, lukewarm or tepid
senses: to be warm, lukewarm or tepid
to glow with love; to be enamored
to be lukewarm or indifferent in feeling
la:verb:tepeo.html:
tĕpĕo, ēre, v. n.
Sanscr. tap, to be warm; tapas, heat; O. H. Germ. damf, warm
,
to be moderately warm, lukewarm, or tepid (very rare; not in Cic.; cf.: caleo, ferveo).
Lit.: ubi (dolium) temperate tepebit,: carnes gallinaceorum ut tepebant avulsae,: ubi plus tepeant hiemes,: cor tepens,: tepentes aurae,; : sole tepente,: truncus tepens,; cf.: tractu (caeli) tepente,.—
Trop.
To be warm or to glow with love, to be enamored: quo (Lycidā) calet juventus Nunc omnis et mox virgines tepebunt,: nescio quem sensi corde tepente deum,.—
To be lukewarm, cool, cold; to be without ardor, indifferent in love, etc.: saepe tepent alii juvenes: ego semper amavi,; so (opp. amare),: affectus tepet, * .

la:verb:tepesco.gloss: to grow warm, to become lukewarm
senses: to grow warm, to become lukewarm
la:verb:tepesco.html:
tĕpesco, pŭi, 3,
v. inch. n. [tepeo], to become moderately warm, lukewarm, or tepid.
To grow warm: maria agitata ventis ita tepescunt, ut, etc., * ; ; : nostra tepescit aqua,: fixo ferrum in pulmone tepescit,; —
To grow cool (rare).
Lit., . —
Trop., to cool off, decrease in ardor: paulatim fugit ira ferox mentesque tepescunt,: negotio tepescente,: cum omnes amicitiae Romae tepescant,: veneres tepuere sub annis,.

la:verb:tepefacio.html:
tĕpĕfăcĭo, fēci, factum, 3 (
fut. scanned tĕpēfăciet, ; cf. liquefacio), v. a.
tepeo - facio
, to make moderately warm, lukewarm, or tepid; to warm, tepefy (class.); as verb. fin. act.: is ejus (solis) tactus est, non ut tepefaciat solum, sed etiam saepe comburat,: corpus,: ova,: linteum,: in matris jugulo ferrum acutum,.—Pass.: medicamentum semper ante tepefieri convenit,: insecta tepefiunt,, 5, § 13.— Part. perf.: umor mollitur tepefactus et tabescit,; ; ; ; ; ; .

la:noun:tepor.html:
tĕpor, ōris, m.
id.
,
a gentle warmth, lukewarmness, tepidity, tepor (cf.: fervor, calor).
Opp. to cold (class.): externus et adventicius tepor,: uvae,: solis,; : mundi,: primus tepor, i. e. of spring,: (cupressus) alibi non nisi in tepore proveniens,in a mild, moderate temperature,; ; : verno tepori similis,: tepore febrium arescunt,.— In plur., ; . —
Concr., plur., fomentations, .—
Opp. to warmth (very rare).
Lit.: excepta vox est, cum teporem incusaret, —
Trop., coldness, languor of language: libri eiusdem lentitudinis ac teporis,
